# OpenWhisper vX.Y.Z

100% local, 100% free, Wispr-Flow-class voice dictation for Mac, Windows, and Linux.

## Download

Pick the installer for your OS from the **Assets** section below.

| OS                        | File                                                         | Notes                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Windows 10 / 11 (x64)     | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_x64_en-US.msi` or `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe` | SmartScreen → "More info" → "Run anyway".                          |
| Windows 11 (ARM64)        | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_arm64_en-US.msi` or `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_arm64-setup.exe` | Same SmartScreen flow.                                             |
| macOS (Apple Silicon)     | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg`                              | Gatekeeper → System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway". |
| macOS (Intel)             | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_x64.dmg`                                  | Same Gatekeeper flow.                                              |
| Linux (x86_64) — Debian/Ubuntu | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb`                            | `sudo dpkg -i OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb`                         |
| Linux (x86_64) — Fedora/RHEL   | `openwhisper-X.Y.Z-1.x86_64.rpm`                         | `sudo dnf install ./openwhisper-X.Y.Z-1.x86_64.rpm`                |
| Linux (x86_64) — Universal     | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage`                       | `chmod +x` and run.                                                |
| Linux (arm64) — all formats    | `OpenWhisper_X.Y.Z_arm64.{deb,rpm,AppImage}`             | As above.                                                          |

**This release is unsigned by design** — OpenWhisper is free software distributed outside any app store, so it doesn't carry an Apple Developer ID or Windows EV certificate. The first-launch warning is a normal part of installing open-source software; after one click your OS won't ask again.

## First-run setup

When you launch OpenWhisper for the first time it will:

1. Ask for accessibility / microphone permission (macOS / Windows).
2. **Auto-download** the speech-to-text model that fits your hardware (~75 MB Whisper Tiny ships with the installer for instant first-use; the larger model arrives in the background).
3. Walk you through a mic test, a hotkey-config step, and a 3-card tutorial.
4. Drop you into the main settings window with the floating widget already visible.

Default hotkey: **Ctrl+Space** (Windows / Linux) or **Option+Space** (macOS).

Default Command Mode hotkey (highlight + speak instruction → rewrite): **Ctrl+Alt+Space** (Windows / Linux) or **Cmd+Ctrl+Space** (macOS).

## Privacy

OpenWhisper performs **all** transcription and AI cleanup locally. Your voice never leaves your machine. The only outbound network calls are:

1. Downloading Whisper / Parakeet / Moonshine model weights from Hugging Face on first run (one-time, no user data).
2. Checking for app updates against this repo's Releases page (opt-out in Settings → About).

The LLM client (`llm_client::validate_local_url`) enforces a hard-coded whitelist of `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `localhost`, `apple-intelligence://`, `phi-silica://`. A bug in user settings cannot leak a transcript to a cloud provider — the network call itself is blocked at the boundary.

## Known limitations

- **macOS / Linux**: the Vibe Coding "backtick-wrap identifiers" pass is a no-op outside Windows because we haven't wired the AX-API / AT-SPI accessibility probes yet. File-tagging (`tag main.py` → `@main.py`) still works on all platforms.
- **Linux Wayland**: keyboard injection via `rdev` doesn't support Wayland. X11 works.
- **Apple Foundation Models / Phi Silica**: backend stubs exist, real FFI is not wired. Use the bundled `llama.cpp` sidecar or install Ollama for local LLM cleanup.
